lines.t: *Napoleon* is *one battle* away from taking back Europe.
What if he had *won* it?
Ten years earlier, he seemed *unbeatable*.
In 1804 he crowns himself *emperor*,
lines.say: In eighteen oh four he crowns himself emperor,

lines.t: and at *Austerlitz* he defeats Austria and Russia in a single day.
By 1812 he controls almost all of continental Europe,
lines.say: By eighteen twelve he controls almost all of continental Europe,

lines.t: from *Madrid* to *Warsaw*.
But then he invades *Russia* with some *600,000 men*.
lines.say: But then he invades Russia with some six hundred thousand men.

lines.t: *Winter*, hunger and disease tear them apart.
Only a *small fraction* makes it back.
After escaping his exile on *Elba*, he returns to power.
At *Waterloo* he faces *Wellington* and *Blücher's* Prussians.
*Rain* delays his attack... and the Prussians arrive just in time.
But imagine the ground dries out *sooner*,
the Prussians are delayed... and Napoleon *wins*.
Plot twist: many historians believe it *still* wouldn't have lasted.
*Austria* and *Russia* were already mobilizing *hundreds of thousands* of soldiers against him.
So what if he had won in *Russia* instead?
Europe would be a *French empire*, with the *Napoleonic Code* and the metric system across the continent.
A kind of *European Union*... a century and a half early.
In reality, he died in exile on *Saint Helena* in 1821.
lines.say: In reality, he died in exile on Saint Helena in eighteen twenty-one.

lines.t: Was Napoleon a *liberator*... or a *tyrant*? Tell me in the comments.
